snippet.textDisplay:
Thank you-describes my experience perfectly! Throughout childhood & into adulthood, i was scapegoated by my mum & sisters (though not by my dad, who was lovely & we were v close). My dad passed at 62 and those siblings who had been preferred by mum, were suddenly nowhere to be found. Yes, mum needed help as she was falling apart but... one felt she couldnt provide that as she had kids & they needed her more, the other felt it would interrupt her social/ life too much. So they both thought that was entirely my responsibility instead. Obviously, i had a difficult relationship with my mum but, dad had passed and she needed someone there, so i did it.
It turned out to be a v beautiful thing, laced with moments of great tenderness and pure love, shared between us. It stayed that way for 13yrs until she then passed. I wouldnt change that for the world. I even took counselling courses up, so as to learn therapeutic tools to help her in her grief (of course, understanding that if i counselled someone i knew, it would be pointless due to the lack of objectivity!). But, i did learn how to be there fully, and be a hand to hold, anyway. I learnt not to have the 'i must fix her' mentality. And it all helped her -in her own time.
My siblings thoughts became instead, on who got what when her time came, which broke her heart and made her feel more valuable to them, dead than alive. These women who shed prized so highly. Im sure you can guess -she left her house to me. Am sure you can guess the outcome-i was disowned by them as a result! They told me it was irrespective of whether i handed it over to them or not at that stage. The fact she had chosen me & not them, was enough! We havent spoken properly in 16yrs. Ive been told they love me and ill always be their 'lovely, kind sister', but they still cant deal with it all so, im to stay away! Hows that for a narc collapse?!

I can ignore all the insidious nastiness that went on throughout our childhood and beyond; the friendships she destroyed; the family events she cut me out of -- but not the stealing. The peculiar thing was that the horrible husband knew exactly what the scheming sister was about, not that he cared, but he understood her far better than I ever did. They are both out of my life now.

snippet.textDisplay:
If it weren’t for the fact that things really didn’t rot, until well into adulthood, I’d say my situation is on the darker side. I’ve often said that I “may” have been the golden child, swapped into the the scapegoat role, because the question is, “Was I?” While I and others may have seen me as my mother’s mini me and my sister as everything but, I’ve become uncertain of its truth or I don’t know exactly when the swap began, although I feel triangulation had been as part of my family dynamic, since we were young.

My situation has been one of, yes, feeling, from a stepbrother and sister-in-law that, “Although we escaped our mothers, you just need to stick it out and be the sacrificial lamb, if for no other reason, because you’re the most likely to ensure everyone gets their slice of the inheritance.” Well, that was their undoing. Wasn’t legally as part of an intestate death. Got nuttin’, ain’t gettin’ nuttin’.

But, what was worse, was that my mother wasn’t ignoring abuse, she was salivating over the idea of it. It said a lot of things. It said, “If I was in good enough shape, I’d do more than sabotage your life, career and livelihood. I do not care what you’ve been to me or what you’ve done for me. I want blind subservience and compliance, for my benefit ONLY and for your demise.” She did say, “You might have to take abuse, from your sister.” She was soothed by saying so and, through the legal process, I have, although I’ve gotten some satisfaction from inheriting my share of the estate, while also making that demon twist in the wind.

But, despite its completely dark side, it has been worth it all, to leave. When I discovered that I simply come from a family, where my mother came to hate and want the worst for me, where my sister felt exponentially so, and where step-siblings only saw me as a meal ticket, and even when I look at extended family, nothing much seems good there either, I’ve been able to have some friggin’ PEACE, from this rather cunning tribe of elders and siblings, most of whom look at me, as simply something to devour, I’m not missing out on ANYTHING.

Not for the status quo. It's easier for them to deny the reality. Deny the pain, deny the issues. The external image doesn't matter (in some cases). It's the thing that they don't want to deal with that problem. Then it's YOUR problem only. Or you are the cause — stop creating problems. Often they are enablers.

I try to avoid contact with my sisters since some years ago. My mother doesn't want to accept it. Things are not solved and I am still dependant (fincancially). Sometimes there are problems — one of my sisters wants something ("needs" something). For example, last year, my oldest sister, who lives in another town, married, "needed" our car in the summer holidays. My mother forced me to "solve" that issue with her (narcissistic and manipulative), whom I was not talking since 2 years before that, and whom I was having troubles when dealing, my mother knowing this, and it ended up, as expected, my mother forcing me to cede.

Now my other sister, who also is "independent" living in another town, has another object. She "asked" me if she could take it (honestly I wonder why she asks me), but the word was on my mother, who was aware that I thought she shouldn't take it. As expected she took it on my mom's permission. Three weeks later, time MORE THAN ENOUGH to have used it, I tell my mother... And again, she says to me "then tell her, ask it to her". My mother knows I have trouble talking to them, I DON'T WANT to talk to them, but my mother denies it. Doesn't allow me to not wanting contact or even having troubles when having to deal with them. Then she doesn't consider at all my needs when my abusive sisters "need" something, so she is the one who decides, deals and has the words, but if I have any issue, then it's on me who has to deal with them.

This is not about an image of the family. My mother is just an enabler who invalidates me. She doesn't want to deal with troubles. She doesn't see it. We are the trouble makers, we create the troubles, whe see and create troubles where there aren't.
